headline: Math benchmarks are nearly saturated while real-work agents lag behind
outlook: Math has nearly run out of headroom, closing 95% of its remaining gap over the past year, with FrontierMath passing 90% in September and GPT-6.1 Sol just posting 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work is the slowest-moving area, closing only 32% of its headroom: GPT-6 Astra sits at 20.8% on the Remote Labor Index and the best OSWorld 2 score is 31.4%, so on current trends neither is expected to reach 90% before 2027. The likely bridge is task length, since the longest tasks AI can handle have reached 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview and have been doubling about every 4.2 months, putting a full 40-hour work-week task most likely around December 2026, though the range stretches to August 2027. Cost is falling just as fast: the price of GPQA-level performance has dropped from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens and, on current trends, could fall under a cent by early 2027. Treat these dates loosely, because past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, with a typical miss of five months.
